mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 5-year averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate environment, which erodes real corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 5-year averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A strong and sustained rise in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both PAYEMS (payroll employment) and UNRATE (unemployment rate) is paradoxical and signals a data inconsistency or a sectoral labor reallocation shock; under such conditions, S&P 500 returns tend to be volatile and are more likely to be negative over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such anomalous months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue for consumer-facing companies and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of strong monetary easing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS declines for three months and monetary easing is not present (t-test p > 0.05).
